## Natural history notes

A small tortricid moth characterized by tan to yellowish-brown forewings with darker brown patches and bands, often forming a bold mask-like pattern that gives it the “Batman” appearance. In Florida, the Batman Moth is part of the state’s moth fauna and belongs to an eastern North American species ranging south to Florida, where it is likely found in wooded, shrubby, and semi-open habitats with suitable host plants. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on host-plant foliage in the typical leafroller manner, using silk to shelter within folded or tied leaves.
